APT_Backdoor_SUNBURST_1.author: FireEye
APT_Backdoor_SUNBURST_1.description: This rule is looking for portions of the SUNBURST backdoor that are vital to how it functions. The first signature fnv_xor matches a magic byte xor that the sample performs on process, service, and driver names/paths. SUNBURST is a backdoor that has the ability to spawn and kill processes, write and delete files, set and create registry keys, gather system information, and disable a set of forensic analysis tools and services.

APT_Dropper_Raw64_TEARDROP_1.description: This rule is looking for portions of the SUNBURST backdoor that are vital to how it functions. The first signature fnv_xor matches a magic byte xor that the sample performs on process, service, and driver names/paths. APT_HackTool_PS1_COSMICGALE_1.author: FireEye
APT_HackTool_PS1_COSMICGALE_1.description: This rule is looking for portions of the SUNBURST backdoor that are vital to how it functions. The first signature fnv_xor matches a magic byte xor that the sample performs on process, service, and driver names/paths. SUNBURST is a backdoor that has the ability to spawn and kill processes, write and delete files, set and create registry keys, gather system information, and disable a set of forensic analysis tools and services.

APT_Webshell_SUPERNOVA_1.author: FireEye
APT_Webshell_SUPERNOVA_1.description: This rule is looking for portions of the SUNBURST backdoor that are vital to how it functions. The first signature fnv_xor matches a magic byte xor that the sample performs on process, service, and driver names/paths. SUNBURST is a backdoor that has the ability to spawn and kill processes, write and delete files, set and create registry keys, gather system information, and disable a set of forensic analysis tools and services.

VULN_KeePass_DB_Brute_Forcible.description: Detects KeePass .kdbx password stores, which could be brute forced to steal the credentials. With AES-KDF and less than 65536 iterations the cracking speed with a single GPU is 20k/s, for the old default of 6.000 iterations it's 200k/s. Best remediation is to change the key derivative function to Argon2d and delete all older versions of the .kdbx
VULN_KeePass_DB_Brute_Forcible.rule_category: Detects KeePass .kdbx password stores, which could be brute forced to steal the credentials. With AES-KDF and less than 65536 iterations the cracking speed with a single GPU is 20k/s, for the old default of 6.000 iterations it's 200k/s. Best remediation is to change the key derivative function to Argon2d and delete all older versions of the .kdbx
